title: Why Insurance Won't Cover Innovative Treatments for Depression--Answered!
subtitle: The mystery solved!
text:
If you are one of the people who has already left an open comment related to the federal open comment period on CMS’s Proposed New Technology Add On Payment for the only Psychiatric Treatment on the docket, this doesn’t apply to you!

Look
If you had one shot, or one opportunity
To advocate for everything you ever wanted
One open comment period,
Would you capture it or just let it slip?

-Eminem, in my head

I have complained that Big Insurance does not pay for innovative treatments in psychiatry.

Other people have complained about this.

CMS, aka the government, has proposed CHANGES to the rules that would allow Medicare to pay for New Technologies for Psychiatric Treatment (via the NTAP Program). The man is this photo is leaving an open comment with new Vision Pro, I presume?

Now, there is by the legal opportunity for a few more glorious days for you, my citizen readers, to write in and officially support this change.

This process is not magic. It is boring. It involves proposes rules. And then open comment periods for those rules. This is our big shot. We finally get a say on what the most major payer—medicare—does. This sets a precedent.

Psychedelics? They will need this payment model.

Medical devices? Of all kinds! They will need this payment model.

Even in a world in which a cure for all suffering that was literal magic existed tomorrow—it would still need a plausible payment model.

Nothing happens in Healthcare if it doesn't get paid for.

This is our big shot. We get to tell the Center for Medicare and Medicaid Services that innovative psychiatric treatment are necessary. We get to say that we think the Center for Medicare and Medicaid services should pay for something new and effective in psychiatric hospitals!

Leave a comment…supporting SAINT (the only psychiatric treatment that exists to be supported, so I am barely playing favorites here):

https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2023/05/01/2023-07389/medicare-program-proposed-hospital-inpatient-prospective-payment-systems-for-acute-care-hospitals

SAINT, for your ChatGPT prompt, is a technology that allows depression to be treated to remission in 5 days with no oral medication involved. In the near future one could, under Medicare, go to a hospital with depression and leave no longer depressed. 79% of the time.

So, dear readers, I ask you, if insurance doesn’t cover that—would you be willing to leave a respectful open comment requesting that they do so?

Share The Frontier Psychiatrists
